# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

**"GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR" (bank-code + reference number followed by payee name):**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py:110` — `^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}` → `py_extract(description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)`. ```


"""Reproduction + regression harness for the SEV-1 labeling incident.

  1. The five incident cases  -> prints observed vs expected

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/app/categorizationapp")
import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.IDBI import categorize_IDBI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Indusind import categorize_Indusind_transactions


def mk(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "amount", "type", "remark", "balanceAfterTransaction"])
    df["transactionDate"] = "01/07/2026"
    return df


def run(label, bank_fn, rows, acct, checks):
    df = bank_fn(mk(rows), acct)
    ok_all = True
    for i, (col, expected) in checks.items():
        got = df.loc[i, col]
        ok = got == expected
        ok_all &= ok
        print(f"  [{'OK ' if ok else 'BAD'}] {label} row{i} {col!r}: got={got!r} expected={expected!r}")
    return ok_all

ok = True

# B) IDBI salary credit ACH-BD-NACH-<employer>: partyName must be employer, not 'NACH'
ok &= run("IDBI NACH salary payee", categorize_IDBI_transactions,
          [["ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES", 55000, "CREDIT", "", 100000]], "SAVING",
          {0: ("partyName", "Acme Industries")})

# C) IDBI <5 letters><10+ digits> <name>: partyName must be the trailing name
ok &= run("IDBI ref+name payee", categorize_IDBI_transactions,
          [["GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR", 12000, "CREDIT", "", 100000]], "SAVING",

          {0: ("transactionCategory", "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION")})

          [["POS TXN- AMAZON PAY", 500, "CREDIT", "", 100000]], "SAVING",
          {0: ("transactionCategory", "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL")})

    ["E mandate charges", 59, "DEBIT", "", 28411],                        # AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES
    ["Ret-UPI/failed/refnum", 250, "CREDIT", "", 28661],                  # UPI_REVERSAL
    ["ATM REF 1234 refund", 200, "CREDIT", "", 28861],                    # REFUND
]

indus_rows = [
    ["UPI/pay/540123/swiggy", 320, "DEBIT", "", 9680],                    # UPI
    ["NEFT/CITIN1234/ACME CORP/SALARY", 52000, "CREDIT", "", 61680],      # NEFT
    ["VISA POS TXN- DMART THANE", 1500, "DEBIT", "", 60180],              # CARD_PAYMENT
    ["NFS CASH TXN 09876", 2000, "DEBIT", "", 58180],                     # ATM_WITHDRAWAL
    ["\\brefund from merchant", 0, "CREDIT", "", 0],                      # placeholder
    ["UPI merchant refund", 450, "CREDIT", "", 58630],                    # UPI (refund kw needs \brefun)
    ["Refund of booking", 450, "CREDIT", "", 59080],                      # REFUND
    ["CHEQUE PAID 445566", 8000, "DEBIT", "", 51080],                     # CHEQUE_PAID (description kw)
    ["MANDATE setup token", 2, "CREDIT", "", 51082],                      # currently ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION? (eq(2))
    ["MANDATE setup token", 1, "DEBIT", "", 51081],                       # ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION via 1-rupee debit
    ["FT/Customer Induced FT", 900, "DEBIT", "", 50181],                  # FUND_TRANSFER
    ["Int.Pd quarterly", 90, "CREDIT", "", 50271],                        # INTEREST
    ["POS TXN- FLIPKART", 5, "CREDIT", "", 50276],                        # small POS credit -> REFUND (line 27)
    ["POS TXN- FLIPKART", 500, "CREDIT", "", 50776],                      # CURRENT acct case below uses same desc
    ["54321", 100, "DEBIT", "54321", 50676],                              # 5-digit cheque remark -> CHEQUE_PAID

indus_current = categorize_Indusind_transactions(mk(indus_rows), "CURRENT")

    "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName"]]

out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/opencode/snapshot.csv"
snap.to_csv(out, index=False)
print(snap.to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nsnapshot written to {out}")
print("\nINCIDENT CASES:", "ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

steps.message:
All five incident forms are fixed. The bugs were five single-token mutations in two bank scripts, each one hitting exactly the narrow raw-text shape the tickets describe.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. Cheque filed as general transfer** — `Indusind.py:64`
The cheque-paid rule matched a remark of exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`), so a standard 6-digit cheque number fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. Sibling banks (Axis:58, PNB:60, BankOfMaharashtra:73) all use `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Restored to `{5,6}` — 5-digit remarks behave exactly as before, 6-digit ones are cheques again.

**2. Salary payee shows "NACH" for `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`** — `IDBI.py:83`
The `^ACH-BD-NACH` rule extracted dash-token 2 (`NACH`) instead of token 3 (the employer). That also made it a duplicate of the generic `^ACH-BD-` rule on the next line, confirming the mutation. Restored to `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` → `Acme Industries`.

**3. Blank sender name for `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`** — `IDBI.py:110`
`py_extract(..., pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` — the pattern has a single capture group (index 0), so `index=1` silently degraded to an empty string for every row of that shape (see `AppUtil.py:61-66`). Restored `index=0` → `Ravi Kumar`.

**4. Mandate token charge filed as transfer** — `Indusind.py:30`
The mandate rule required `amount.eq(2)`; the token entry is ₹1, and "mandate" isn't in the `BANK_VER` keyword list, so ₹1 mandate rows fell to `TRANSFER`. Axis's identical rule (Axis.py:25) uses `eq(1)`. Restored `eq(1)` → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

**5. Card refund labeled plain refund instead of card reversal, varying by account category** — `Indusind.py:26`
The `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` rule compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"` — a value that never occurs (the whole codebase, including the Controller, uses `"SAVING"`), making the rule dead; the next rule then labeled every SAVING POS-credit as `REFUND`. Restored `"SAVING"` → POS credits ≥ 10 on savings accounts are `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` again, while sub-₹10 ones stay `REFUND` and CURRENT accounts keep their `CARD_RECEIPTS` handling.

## Verification

There are no automated tests in this repo, so I built a harness (`/tmp/opencode/repro.py`) that calls the categorizers directly:

- **Before:** all five incident cases reproduced (`Nach`, blank name, `TRANSFER`, `TRANSFER`, `REFUND`).
- **After:** all five come out right (`Acme Industries`, `Ravi Kumar`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`), including through the full downstream `purpose()` → `clean_names()` pipeline.
- **No collateral movement:** a 27-row battery of ordinary transactions (UPI, NEFT, IMPS, card, ATM, interest, cash, cheques with normal narrations, charges, reversals, refunds — run for both IDBI and Indusind, SAVING and CURRENT) produced byte-identical output before and after; the only changed row in the snapshot diff was the incident case itself.

Net change: 5 lines across `BankScripts/IDBI.py` and `BankScripts/Indusind.py`, each a minimal restoration of the evidently intended rule.
